output.myth: Skeru was a raven who sat on the highest stake of Hesk's Reel and put questions to the wind all day. Is the herring running? Is the goat-boy home? Where does the string end? Tavo heard her, and since he laughs at everything he took the questions off her beak and flung them out over the cliffs. Some came back as weather. That is why old women who ask the sky too often are answered, and why the answers are cold. Aun, who cut the string, once asked Skeru the same thing, and she gave him no reply, only a black wing lifted toward the Upper Sea. She is still up there with her wings open, asking. Mend your nets, and when you ask the wind, ask once.
output.verse:
Skeru asks the wind
how far does the string go down
the wind answers: cold
